name: Hollywood Cerise
lede: Hollywood Cerise is a vivid pink-magenta that carried the name "Hollywood" alone for two decades before anyone added the word cerise.

sections.title: A name that grew a second word
sections.body:
*Cerise* is French for cherry, and entered English as a color word in the nineteenth century; the Oxford English Dictionary's earliest citation is The Times, 30 November 1858 [1]. This particular pink-magenta is older than that borrowing: our library traces the plain name "Hollywood" to 1922, decades before "Hollywood Cerise" is recorded [1]. The fuller name appears by the 1940s, and by the 1950s the Venus Paradise brand sold a colored pencil under exactly that name [1].

Its nearest named neighbors are [[frostbite]], [[hollywood-cerise]] and [[persian-rose]], all close enough to read as the same family at a glance [2]. [[deep-pink]] sits a little further out, and [[barbie-pink]] further still, duller and lighter [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive has a color within CIEDE2000 4 of Hollywood Cerise covering at least 1 percent of its canvas, as photographed [3]. That describes the museum collections behind our archive, not painting as a whole: a magenta this saturated is rare in oil paint before modern synthetic dyes and inks, and our archive is thin on anything made with those [3].

origin.named_after: Hollywood, California; the word cerise added later
